stateRatePct.note: Delaware has no sales tax. It charges a one-time document fee when a vehicle is titled. The statute sets $5.25 for each $100 of the purchase price, and the state announced the change from 4.25% to 5.25% on Oct 1, 2025. The statute rounds to the nearest dollar and has lower flat amounts under $500.

sources.title: Delaware Code, Title 30, Chapter 30 - Motor vehicle document fee

tradeInReducesBase.note: The purchase price is the gross price less any trade-in or allowance. With no trade-in, a private sale of another vehicle within 60 days before or after the title date earns the same credit.

outOfStateCredit.note: A vehicle bought and registered in another state is exempt from the document fee if a sales, transfer or similar tax was paid there within 90 days before Delaware titling. This is a full exemption, not a credit, so it is not calculated here.

notes: The document fee is rounded to the nearest dollar and is lower in flat amounts for prices under $500; the calculator uses a straight 5.25%.

content.intro: {state} has no sales tax. It charges a one-time document fee of {stateRate} of the purchase price when you title a vehicle, plus a flat title fee and a yearly registration fee.

howItWorks.text: The document fee is {stateRate} of the purchase price. A trade-in lowers the price, and so does a sale of another vehicle within a set window if you have no trade-in.
If you bought and registered the vehicle in another state and paid a sales or similar tax there recently, the document fee may not apply.
The state announced an increase of the document fee from a lower rate to the current one in a recent fee change.

faq.q: Does Delaware have a sales tax on cars?
faq.text: No. It charges a document fee on the purchase price when a vehicle is titled.

faq.q: Does a trade-in lower the document fee?
faq.text: Yes, the purchase price is the gross price less any trade-in or allowance.
